chapter: Chicago and Oliver's band in California
title: Union trial and the break-up of Oliver's band
summary: The union case over Oliver sending for Baby Dodds, two weeks' notice pay, fines, and Garland deciding to stay in California.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So, you know, alright. Baby Dots was playing in St. Louis. He wrote to Baby Dots. And he said for Baby Dots. Now, he didn't get permission from the union. Number six, you see. Baby Dots. Baby Dots. After he sent for Baby Dots, we went down to the union and reported it. Ram did. Oh, he called in Joe. He called Joe in. He went to the trial board. He had me there and Ram there. Cause he asked me questions. I told him, yeah. Told him how it just happened. They found out that Baby Dots was unfinancial. In the union, you see. Back there in St. Louis. And the next thing, he didn't get permission from the union to report to Baby Dots here in San Francisco. He said, you can't report nobody to have it out of the consultant board. Joe said, well, they ain't got nobody here to play my music. He said, well, you don't know that. He said, well, you come to find out. He said, I want a jazz drummer. Dixie Lanzo. He said, well, I'm sorry you didn't come and notify us that you were going to make a change. In the first place, you didn't give the man a notice. You didn't give even one of them a notice. He said, I didn't find the other fella. He said if he let him go, he was going to go. He said, there's that in black and white. No. He said, well, he ain't gone yet then. He said, I want either one of these go. Give him two weeks notice, you see. And now he had to get $400 if he let him go. Joe Alba had to pay both of them bars $400. Two weeks notice, you know.

And, oh yeah, he was getting $200 a man. A week. In those days, man. So, they find, what did they find Joe? They find, I think they found Joe $500. And Joe, I don't know if Joe ever paid any of it here or there. But when Joe left, you understand? We'd come on back down to Los Angeles. We'd come down there to play two nights for Jelly Roll out to the jump study. Not jump study, Leakes Lake. And we'd play Saturday to Sunday. So, on Monday, we'd all meet up at Tootie's. At my house, you know. We're going, we're going back. We're going to New York. All right, fellas. Nobody was satisfied with me. I didn't answer. I said, what's the matter with you, Pops? I said, well, Joe, you don't need me hitting around the bushes. I said, I ain't going back to New York. Why? I said, I can get my shoes shined a whole year around in California. And I can't get it back there in New York. I'm tired of fighting all that snow. Oh, he jumped, oh, he cussed me out. Then got to be a native now. Got you a chick out your neck. I said, sure, I got a chick. Ain't you got one? What's the matter with me? Is this final? I said, sure, I mean that. All right. I don't know. They kept on coming back, coming back, all of them in the band. Man, come on. Don't, don't, don't, don't leave the band. I said, no, I ain't going back. I didn't go back. But they got Bill. Bill Johnson. Joe went back to New York and come back. He's laying for them. He come back to Chicago. You see, he hadn't paid. They put the international on to Joe. He got into New York and said, Chicago. And he's going to open up. Don't forget the name of the dance hall. Oh, it was a big night that night. The bar was ready. Joe was up there with his dance hall. Joe was up there with his dance hall. And he was going to open up. And he was going to open up. And he was going to open up. Big night that night. The bar was ready. Joe was up there with his 10 piece band, you know. Business agent walked in there before they got set up good. They all come and tell him, nobody play a lick. Don't, don't take those instruments out of your case. Well, as the proprietor, and this woman was running, they told us, the only way that band could play there that night, she had to lay down $500. $500. All these men right here, as far as suspended, as in this band. And they didn't know nothing. Half of them didn't know nothing about what happened in San Francisco, you know. But as he was playing with Joe, you see, they spent all of them. And they were going to get $500. Come up with $500. Got it.
You know, I'm going to let you talk too long. Let me ask you one more question and then we'll cover. Okay?
